CLAUDE.md

Source: AGENTS.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/native-code.md @.claude/shared/correctness.md @.claude/shared/assurance.md

AGENTS.md is a symlink to this file, so other agents read the same text; they do not follow the @ imports above, which name the files to read.

What this is

mdbx is an R binding to libmdbx, an embedded transactional key-value store, vendored and compiled into the package. The licence is MIT; libmdbx is Apache-2.0.

The exported API mirrors the C API: mdbx_env_*, mdbx_txn_*, mdbx_dbi_* and bare mdbx_get/mdbx_put/mdbx_del. Storage is bytes; a missing key reads as NULL. Keys and values go in as a raw vector or a single string stored as UTF-8, and come back decoded as text unless as = "raw", settled in Stage 4, following clibmdbx. Serialization of R objects is deliberately not the engine layer’s job. Durability was settled in Stage 5.6, also following clibmdbx: flags pass through by name (flags = c("SAFE_NOSYNC", ...)) rather than through a curated enum, and nothing is relaxed by default. Database handle representation was settled in Stage 8: a name re-resolved per transaction, never cached across one, because an aborted transaction poisons a MDBX_dbi.

0.1.0 shipped: the vendored build, env open/close with flags and geometry, read/write transactions, get/put/delete, named databases with per-database stat, listing, dropping and sequences, ordered and resumable key/item scans, stat/info/limits, routine registration, three-platform builds, and the lifecycle, fork and panic tests. Cursors, batch entry points (mdbx_get_many() and friends), duplicate keys (DUPSORT), and serialization are 0.2: see the Feature gap against clibmdbx section of .agents/roadmap.md, which ranks them by implementation cost.

Four questions remain open and should not be settled unilaterally: where serialization lives, how much of the cursor API to expose, map resizing, and the on-disk layout beyond the subdir default. .agents/design.md has the reasoning for each.

.agents/ holds four documents, and nothing in them repeats what the code already says. .agents/roadmap.md is the staged plan through 0.1.0 with the per-stage findings, the feature gap against clibmdbx ranked by cost, the Open questions table, and the upstream reference links: start here, and respect what it defers to 0.2. Unlike the shared convention, its headings carry status (— **DONE**). .agents/design.md records why each API question was answered the way it was, including the four still open; read the relevant decision before revisiting one. .agents/vendoring.md covers the pin, the build flags and the patch series. .agents/formal-verification.md is a proposal to specify the lifecycle and transaction protocol as a Lean state machine.

Current state

0.1.2 is on CRAN, published on 23 October 2026 (crandb, verified 2026-11-11). Its history explains much of the build:

  • 0.1.0 was accepted on 27 September 2026, at the third upload. CRAN’s clang-UBSAN, gcc-UBSAN and M1-SAN checks then reported undefined behaviour in the bundled libmdbx.
  • 0.1.1 was the fix, published on 28 September 2026.
  • 0.1.1 was archived on 19 October 2026 for CRAN’s valgrind reports (#30).
  • 0.1.2 fixes those, in the bundled libmdbx (patches 0007–0009).

Every stage of the roadmap through Stage 7 (release hardening) is done, Stage 8 (named databases, pulled into 0.1.0) included; Stage 9 is a proposal. The default branch carries 0.1.2.9000, whose one change so far makes libmdbx compile on Windows arm64 (patch 0010).

Environments live in src/r_mdbx.cpp + R/env.R, transactions in R/txn.R, get/put/del in R/data.R, named databases in R/dbi.R, stat/info in R/stat.R, key listing in R/scan.R, environment/transaction flags in src/r_flags.cpp + R/flags.R, the concurrency contract in R/concurrency.R, and condition classes in R/conditions.R.

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is #33, v0.1.3. The cran-release reminder #35 opens from 2026-12-04, six weeks after 0.1.2. 0.2 is the release whose scope is the roadmap’s Feature gap section, cursors first.

dastash imports mdbx (>= 0.1.1) from CRAN. A change to the R API or to the on-disk behaviour reaches it.

Commands

Rscript -e 'devtools::document()'                     # roxygen2 + cpp11::cpp_register()
Rscript -e 'testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-txn.R")'
R CMD INSTALL --preclean .                            # exercise src/Makevars directly
tools/update-libmdbx.sh                               # re-vendor upstream, replay the patches
tools/interop-check.sh                                # round trip with clibmdbx; needs python3, network

After adding a [[cpp11::register]] function, confirm R/cpp11.R actually gained the wrapper: devtools::document() has been observed to skip cpp11::cpp_register().

devtools, roxygen2, testthat, pkgbuild, and rcmdcheck are installed against R 4.6. tools/interop-check.sh is a maintainer script, not part of R CMD check: run it when bumping the vendored libmdbx, alongside tools/update-libmdbx.sh. It proves a database this package writes is readable by an independently built libmdbx, and the reverse, which nothing in the suite can catch.

Architecture

Everything ships in one shared object

libmdbx is vendored as the official amalgamation into src/vendor/libmdbx/ and compiled into the package’s own mdbx.so/mdbx.dll. The amalgamation is three files: mdbx.c includes mdbx-internals.h alongside mdbx.h. There is no submodule, no CMake, no system libmdbx, and no separately dlopen’d library. This is what makes CRAN builds work: the tarball is self-contained and R CMD SHLIB is the only build system.

src/Makevars sets PKG_CPPFLAGS = -Ivendor/libmdbx -D__dll_export= -DMDBX_BUILD_FLAGS='"R-CMD-SHLIB"' -DMDBX_ENV_CHECKPID=1 -DMDBX_TXN_CHECKOWNER=1 -DMDBX_UNALIGNED_OK=0 and PKG_LIBS = -pthread, and lists every object by hand: cpp11.o r_flags.o r_mdbx.o r_mdbx_hooks.o vendor/libmdbx/mdbx.o. src/Makevars.win repeats it with -D_WIN32_WINNT=0x0A00 (mandatory: a non-DLL libmdbx build fails with an #error without it), -DWIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN=1, -DNOMINMAX=1 and PKG_LIBS = -lntdll -ladvapi32 -luser32. Both files explain every flag in their comments.

The non-obvious flags:

  • -D__dll_export= (empty) stops libmdbx marking its symbols dllexport on Windows, so the MDBX API does not leak out of the package DLL alongside the registered routines.
  • MDBX_ENV_CHECKPID / MDBX_TXN_CHECKOWNER make MDBX detect cross-process and cross-thread misuse, important because parallel::mclapply(), future, and callr can carry an open environment across a fork().
  • MDBX_UNALIGNED_OK=0 keeps libmdbx from dereferencing misaligned pointers, which CRAN’s UBSAN flavors reported against 0.1.0.

cpp11 at the boundary, C underneath

The binding layer uses cpp11 (not Rcpp, not hand-written C); the vendored mdbx.c stays plain C. mdbx.h has extern "C" guards, and R links with the C++ driver automatically once a .cpp is present, so the mix needs no extra configuration. First-party source is src/r_mdbx.cpp / src/r_mdbx.h (bindings, mdbx_r::check() error translation), src/r_flags.cpp (the flag vocabulary, which owns the name-to-bit mapping so it cannot drift from the vendored header), and src/r_mdbx_hooks.cpp / .h (the panic and logging boundary the vendored source is patched to call).

Two reasons, both worth more as the batch APIs land. Unwind safety: Rf_error() longjmps and skips destructors; cpp11 routes R API calls through R_UnwindProtect and wraps every entry point in BEGIN_CPP11/END_CPP11, so the stack unwinds and the R jump resumes at the .Call() boundary. Protection bookkeeping: cpp11::sexp and writable:: types protect via a preserve list, removing manual PROTECT/UNPROTECT counting from code that builds many vectors in a loop.

Keep C++ at the boundary only: conversion, result construction, error translation, lifetimes. The MDBX-touching logic stays procedural against the C API.

Registration is generated. cpp11::cpp_register() (run by devtools::load_all() and document()) scans src/*.cpp for [[cpp11::register]] and writes src/cpp11.cpp (call table plus R_init_mdbx, which already emits R_useDynamicSymbols(dll, FALSE) and R_forceSymbols(dll, TRUE)) and R/cpp11.R (internal .Call() wrappers). There is no src/init.c. R/mdbx-package.R declares @useDynLib mdbx, .registration = TRUE.

cpp11::external_pointer<T, Deleter> handles finalizers but constructs with a nil protected field, so parent retention needs an explicit R_SetExternalPtrProtected(); its copy constructor shallow-duplicates the pointer and would double-register a finalizer, so treat these handles as move-only.

Ownership is the hard part

MDBX_env *, MDBX_txn *, and MDBX_cursor * each become an R external pointer with a finalizer. The native hierarchy is env → txn → cursor, and a child must never outlive its parent. The child external pointer therefore retains its parent via the protected/tag fields, so GC cannot free them in the wrong order. Finalizers must be idempotent and defensive.

Transactions end three ways (commit, abort, finalize); after commit/abort the external pointer must be invalidated so later R calls fail cleanly instead of dereferencing freed memory. Cursors track both explicit close and the owning transaction ending.

Keep the native layer thin, but batch at the C level

The lowest-level API operates on raw vectors: MDBX stores bytes, and serialization policy is deliberately kept out of the engine layer. Any encoding/serialization convenience belongs in a higher R layer.

Per-call .Call() overhead dominates for millions of small operations, so batch entry points (mdbx_get_many, mdbx_put_many, mdbx_delete_many) must loop in C, never as an R loop around .Call(). This is the main performance lesson recorded from the reference bindings.

Errors

A central mdbx_check(rc) helper translates MDBX status codes to R conditions via cpp11::stop() (printf-style, throws rather than longjmping), preserving the original code. Not every non-MDBX_SUCCESS status is an error: “key not found” is expected to surface as NULL rather than a condition.

Reference bindings

Two Python bindings are used as prior art, and the design deliberately follows one of them:

  • jyj117/mdbx-py (clibmdbx): the model to follow. Vendored amalgamation pinned to a stable release with recorded SHA-256s, compiled into a single extension. Its macro set and Windows link libraries are the source of the Makevars above.
  • wtdcode/mdbx-py: explicitly rejected. Git submodule + CMake producing a standalone shared library loaded via ctypes. Both halves are unusable in an R package: a submodule does not survive R CMD build, and CRAN builders will not run CMake.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • An environment supports a single transaction at a time, because libmdbx binds transactions to their thread and R is single-threaded. Closing an environment under a live transaction is a documented SIGSEGV, so env_handle keeps a registry of live transactions and mdbx_env_close() refuses while it is non-empty.
  • Handles do not survive fork(). Both handle structs record the pid that created them, and every entry point plus every finalizer refuses a handle reached from another process. This is not belt-and-braces: before Stage 6 added it, any operation on an inherited environment aborted the child, because MDBX_ENV_CHECKPID only notices once a call has already dereferenced the mapping libmdbx drowned in its after-fork hook. Never add an entry point that reaches handle->env without going through env_from_sexp() / txn_from_sexp().
  • Never relax UBSan’s alignment check in CI to get past a misaligned access in libmdbx again. A local -fno-sanitize=alignment once hid exactly what CRAN then reported against 0.1.0; the fix belongs at the source (MDBX_UNALIGNED_OK=0, tools/patches/0006).
  • Do not set -O3, -flto, or visibility flags in Makevars: CRAN forbids packages overriding R’s own optimization flags. Leave CFLAGS to R. No -Wno-* either: Writing R Extensions treats it as non-portable, so a warning is fixed by a patch instead (0004).
  • OBJECTS is hand-listed in both Makevars files, because R only globs src/ itself: keep it in sync when adding a source file. all: stays the first rule, so the clean rule that removes the vendored object (which R CMD build would otherwise ship) cannot become make’s default goal.
  • Never edit src/cpp11.cpp or R/cpp11.R by hand; they are generated.
  • Never hand-edit the vendored sources. Add or change a patch, regenerate, and update the post-patch digests (see Vendored native code).

Testing

  • tests/testthat/ has one file per area (test-env.R, test-txn.R, test-data.R, test-dbi.R, test-stat.R, test-scan.R, test-flags.R, test-limits.R, test-errors.R, test-version.R, test-package.R), plus test-fork.R, test-process.R, test-native-safety.R and the three test-state-machine*.R files.
  • test-process.R needs the package installed (it spawns Rscript), so it skips under devtools::test() and runs under R CMD check.
  • The generated sequences in test-state-machine*.R run public API calls against both the package and a reference model and compare the whole observable state after every step. The model in helper-state-model.R is the oracle, written from the documentation; helper-state-runner.R generates and runs the sequences. They are skip_on_cran(), because the package’s limits vary by page size and a sequence that walks into a boundary could fail on one CRAN machine alone.
  • Helpers: helper-env.R (throwaway paths and environments), helper-fork.R (whether this session can fork(): not on Windows, nor under Positron), helper-keys.R (big-endian integer keys, because byte order is the only order libmdbx has), helper-subprocess.R (separate R processes, since concurrency in libmdbx is between processes).
  • The suite pins map_size (test_map_size, 8 MiB, in helper-env.R). libmdbx’s default reserves about 1.6x physical RAM of address space per environment, and under valgrind every open would negotiate that reservation down. The default geometry is still exercised, once, in test-env.R.

Continuous integration

  • R-CMD-check.yaml calls r-actions’ r-cmd-check.yml@v1: the runners on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu (release/oldrel-1), plus a Windows R-devel row (CRAN’s incoming pretest runs on Debian and Windows R-devel), and the containers matching CRAN’s r-devel Linux flavours, ubuntu-clang (clang 23, C built as -std=gnu23) and ubuntu-gcc16. The container half is the leg that would have caught the C23 keyword-macro warnings before CRAN did; no GitHub runner is that combination. Both halves fail on a WARNING. There is deliberately no R-devel Ubuntu row, because the containers are R-devel on Linux already. It passes --compact-vignettes=gs+qpdf to build. It has no paths-ignore, deliberately: --as-cran checks the URLs in README.md, which ships in the tarball.
  • native-checks.yaml calls sanitizers.yml (UBSan on a runner plus the R-hub clang-asan and gcc-asan containers; gcc-asan’s bounds-strict is the one that sees libmdbx’s trailing-array struct hacks), lto.yml, gctorture.yml, rchk.yml (cpp11 through github-packages) and cran-special.yml (CRAN’s rcnst, rlibro and vnu checks, full runs only). It skips prose with a paths-ignore list rather than the changes.yml gate (#37 tracks gating).
    • shuffled-tests (own) runs the suite shuffled under three seeds, with NOT_CRAN set explicitly so the state machine has one job it is guaranteed to run in.
    • valgrind (own, not r-actions’ valgrind.yml) matches CRAN’s valgrind check: valgrind 3.27.1 built from source (Ubuntu’s 3.22 was green where CRAN’s run of 0.1.1 was not), CRAN’s options exactly, no suppression file, and tools/valgrind/fake-ram.c preloaded so sysconf() reports 256 GB, the machine class whose default-geometry opens failed in #30. tools/valgrind/scan-logs.py prints the ERROR SUMMARY lines.
  • coverage.yaml calls coverage.yml, pinned by commit (it commits the badge). .covrignore leaves out src/vendor, about 22k expressions against 1k of first-party source.
  • pkgdown.yaml builds the site from vignettes/articles/.

Vendored native code

  • Library: libmdbx, Apache-2.0, pinned at v0.14.3 (stable, published 2026-08-09), amalgamation v0.14.3-0-g251562b2, from https://github.com/erthink/libmdbx. The tag object, commit and SHA-256 of every vendored file are in .agents/vendoring.md, with the update procedure.
  • Licence files: LICENSE, NOTICE and COPYRIGHT under src/vendor/libmdbx/. inst/COPYRIGHTS describes the patch series in prose and is what ships as the Apache-2.0 section 4(b) notice, because tools/ is .Rbuildignored and maintainer-only. Authors@R credits Leonid Yuriev, Howard Chu, Symas Corporation and Martin Hedenfalk.
  • Patches: the tree is not pristine. Ten patches in tools/patches/ route libmdbx’s panic and logging through R’s API, drop nine #pragma diagnostic ignored lines, sidestep a false-positive -Warray-bounds from Rtools’ MinGW headers, keep the pre-C23 bool/nullptr macros from shadowing the C23 keywords, turn three trailing-array struct hacks into forms gcc’s -fsanitize=bounds-strict accepts, retry a refused mmap() reservation smaller (valgrind refuses libmdbx’s RAM-scaled default), stop GC records carrying uninitialised bytes to disk, expose where an environment’s page-number lists start, and let the SEH fault handler compile on Windows arm64.
  • They are applied by the maintainer during a version bump, never at build time: tools/update-libmdbx.sh re-vendors and replays the series. tools/patches/README.md is the authoritative record and holds the post-patch digests; the Local patches section of .agents/vendoring.md carries the narrative: what each patch does, and which alternatives were rejected.
